teaser.en: Its leaves are perfectly round, like strands of spaghetti waving under the sea.

summary.en: Noodle seagrass is a flowering plant of shallow subtidal sand, easy to know by its round, spaghetti-like leaves. Like other seagrasses, its meadows shelter the fish and octopus that coastal fishers rely on.

about.en: Noodle seagrass is a true flowering plant that lives fully submerged in the sea. Unlike most seagrasses, which have flat leaves, its leaves are round in cross-section, thin and smooth like strands of spaghetti or noodles. They grow in tufts from creeping stems in the sand and can form dense, waving meadows.

where.en: It grows on shallow subtidal sand, just below the lowest tides, so it is usually covered by water. Seagrass meadows fringe Gazi Bay, Diani-Chale and Vanga-Shimoni. Snorkellers in the lagoons see it best, its noodle-like leaves drifting in the current.

uses.en: Its meadows are habitat for the rabbitfish, parrotfish, octopus and sea cucumbers that Digo fishers depend on. The meadows also trap sediment and help to protect beaches.

names.en: No Digo name has been recorded yet. Swahili speakers usually call sea plants in general *mwani*. In English it is noodle seagrass, and its scientific name is *Syringodium isoetifolium*.

conservation.en: The seagrass meadows of Gazi Bay, Diani-Chale and Vanga-Shimoni are feeding grounds for dugongs, green turtles and rabbitfish, and nurseries for young fish.

sources: Vanga Blue Forest Project Design Document (Plan Vivo, 2019) https://sustainabletravel.org/wp-content/uploads/Vanga-Blue-Forest-PDD_27dec19_PlanVivo.pdf
